one_line_contribution: That a retrieved memory item's marginal value is a property of the (item, instruction) pair rather than of the item — operationalized by splitting both texts into atomic guidance units and labeling each item unit against the instruction as redundant/novel/conflicting — together with a token-matched unit-level surgical ablation, a decoy-instruction placebo, and a retrieval rule that maximizes instruction-conditional novel-unit yield per token.
closest_prior_work: The cluster the proposal never cites: prompt/context compression conditioned on the surrounding prompt — LongLLMLingua and LLMLingua-2, RECOMP, Selective Context, Provence, CompAct. Those systems already delete spans of retrieved context that add nothing given the rest of the prompt, at matched token budgets, and report exactly the headline result of Prediction 3 (accuracy preserved at roughly half the injected tokens). The proposal's defense would be that they condition on the query while it conditions on the instruction, but in an agent scaffold the instruction is simply part of the conditioning prompt those compressors already see, so the delta is a choice of reference span rather than a new mechanism. Sufficient Context (cited) is the conceptual predecessor and AtomMem (cited) supplies the entailment-dedup machinery; between them plus the compression literature, what remains genuinely new is the two-instruction relationality manipulation and the decoy placebo, not the redundant/novel/conflicting axis itself. The Related Work section's failure to engage compression at all reads, to a skeptical AC, as the novelty case not having been tested where the idea actually lives.
strongest_objection: The entire Part 2/Part 3 prediction set presupposes a memory bank with several points of exploitable net effect, and the design does not guarantee one. The track's own prior measurement in this setup is 0 fixes and 6-7 breaks — net effect near zero or slightly negative — and the precheck gate only requires the bank to move >=6% of dev instances 'in either direction', which is churn, not gain. If S1-S0 is ~0 under both instructions (the modal outcome given that prior result), then S2, S3, S4 and S7 are all interventions on an intervention that did nothing: 'S3 loses >=5 points relative to S2' and 'S4 loses >=5 points of fixes relative to S2' are arithmetically near-impossible when there are not 5 points of memory-derived accuracy in the system to remove, and the honest report becomes a bundle of 'inconclusive' rows that the proposal pre-labels a 'clean negative supporting the budget account'. That is not a publishable negative; it is a null about a taxonomy that was never given anything to explain. Second, and independently: Prediction 1 (relationality) is confounded. I_long differs from I_short in content overlap with the bank AND in length AND in baseline accuracy — a GEPA-optimized instruction raises S0, shrinking the fixable set, so a >=5-point collapse in paired gain S1-S0 is precisely what a headroom/ceiling account predicts with zero relationality. The decoy instruction, which is the right control for this, is spent in S7 on the surgery arm and never used as a third instruction condition where it is actually needed. Third, the manipulation has n=1 instruction per condition (one optimizer run, one hand-written prompt); every McNemar test treats instances as the unit while the treatment of interest is the instruction, so no inference generalizes over instructions. The 3-seed optimizer sweep that was cut for budget was the only replication of the study's central manipulation. Fourth, the redundancy is manufactured: I_long is optimized on the same 300 training instances the ExpeL bank is written from, so the label-distribution half of Prediction 1 is close to tautological and the Part 3 method operates in a redundancy regime engineered by shared provenance rather than one that occurs in deployment.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Add a third instruction condition I_decoy_long — length-, register- and token-matched to I_long but optimized on a disjoint split or task so it cannot absorb bank content — and restate Prediction 1 as a difference-in-differences: the gain drop under I_long minus the gain drop under I_decoy_long. Without this the relationality claim is not separable from length and ceiling effects. (2) Produce I_long from >=3 optimizer seeds so the instruction is a replicated unit; report the between-instruction variance rather than treating a single optimizer output as a condition. (3) Re-gate the precheck on net paired effect, not churn: require |S1-S0| >= the stated MDE under at least one instruction before spending 20k episodes, and pre-register what is reported if the bank is inert. (4) Add an off-the-shelf instruction-conditioned compressor and a per-instance oracle subset as the two endpoints for S2 and for Part 3, so the reader can see how much of the achievable headroom the taxonomy captures. (5) Build I_long from a split disjoint from the bank's write split, so redundancy is discovered rather than constructed. (6) Estimate instance difficulty from seeds held out of the S0 arm used for pairing; as written, difficulty is derived from the same S0 runs that define the fix/break outcome, which mechanically correlates the regressor with the response. (7) State an inter-human kappa floor alongside the NLI-human >0.6 gate — 'redundant' between imperative guidance units is a construct humans may not agree on, and NLI-human agreement cannot exceed what inter-human agreement permits; DeBERTa-MNLI is also out of distribution on imperatives, where general instructions fail to entail specific heuristics that are nonetheless behaviorally redundant.
missing_baseline: An off-the-shelf prompt/context compressor applied to the retrieved items with the instruction as conditioning context, at matched injected-token budget (LongLLMLingua / LLMLingua-2, RECOMP, or Provence). This is the deployed alternative to S2 and to the Part 3 selection rule, it is cheap to run, and it is absent from both the baseline list and the related work — the cheap embedding-overlap proxy is not a substitute, since a reviewer's question is not 'does a cheaper feature work' but 'does an existing compressor already do this'. Also missing: a per-instance oracle best-subset upper bound, without which a null in Part 3 cannot be distinguished from 'there was nothing to select'.
preprint_collision: Unusually specific for a collision check — seven named items, explicit verdicts, and an honest caveat about unindexed OpenReview 2026 — and it correctly identifies that the ACL 2026 experience-following study removes the right to claim the phenomenon. Two problems. First, it searched only the agent-memory-harm niche and reports nothing from the neighborhoods where the idea actually lives: context/prompt compression (LLMLingua family, RECOMP, Provence, CompAct), retrieval-vs-parametric-knowledge gating (Adaptive-RAG, self-knowledge-guided retrieval, 'when not to retrieve'), and the knowledge-conflict literature — the CONFLICTING channel is context-memory knowledge conflict under a new name, and not one paper from that line is cited. A search that covers only the area where you expect to be safe has not established novelty. Second, the check itself discloses that the skill-library dedup citations in the previous draft (SkillZip / SkillRAE / SkillOps) 'was not re-confirmed by this search' — i.e., an earlier version of this proposal cited work that may not exist. That materially lowers confidence in the unverifiable arXiv identifiers carried here (2605.09330, 2606.19847, 2601.07470, 2607.05936); each should be verified by title and abstract in the paper, and the collision check should state which were retrieved versus recalled. I did not find a preprint making this exact claim, but on the evidence presented the search is not broad enough for the proposal's novelty claim to be taken as established.
